Article Title: ‘UN experts are oxymoron’: Rubio calls anti-EC protests ‘domestic political matter’
Article Text:
Marco Rubio says Washington will not comment on India's handling of anti-EC protests, leaving the matter to Indians to decide

India rejects UN experts' allegations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday dismissed the term “UN experts” as an “oxymoron” when asked about the United Nations' criticism of India's handling of anti-Election Commission protests, calling the issue a "domestic political matter" that should be decided by Indians.Asked about protests by opposition parties and students in India and UN experts' allegations of a crackdown on demonstrators, Rubio said Washington would not interfere in the country's internal politics."Well the UN experts, my favourite. The UN experts is an oxymororn," he said.He added that India was a democracy with elections and said he would not comment on its domestic political matters.“No, it's a domestic political matter. This is a democracy, they have elections here. I am not going to opine on their political matters,” Rubio said.Rubio distinguished peaceful demonstrations from riots involving vandalism and destruction of property, saying the ability to express differing political opinions was an important feature of democratic societies."I am not talking about the riots, what you see in Europe. They are vandalizing and breaking and burning down buildings. I am not talking about that," he said.Rubio's remarks come amid a diplomatic exchange over concerns raised by UN experts about India's handling of protests. The experts had alleged restrictions on peaceful assembly and raised concerns over the alleged excessive use of force against demonstrators and reports of enforced disappearances.India pushed back against the criticism at the United Nations on Tuesday, rejecting what it described as attempts to portray the country negatively on the basis of unverified allegations and incomplete statistics.Indian diplomat Barkha Tamrakar told the UN that constitutional safeguards, including Article 21, protect human rights and ensure due process.“India firmly opposes any attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics, or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterization of the world's largest democracy,” Tamrakar said.“Human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting,” she added.India also called for impartial and evidence-based engagement on human rights, arguing against what it described as selective scrutiny of countries.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio says Washington will not comment on India's handling of anti-Election Commission protests. Rubio calls UN experts' allegations of a crackdown on demonstrators an "oxymoron" He says the issue is a "domestic political matter" that should be decided by Indians.

Article Title: ‘Get your facts straight’: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of hypocrisy over RSS remarks on women’s rights
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks accusing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of gender inequality, with party leaders alleging hypocrisy and questioning his understanding of the organisation.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan accused the Raebareli MP of hypocrisy over his comments on respecting women, while party MLA Ram Kadam said the Congress leader should study the RSS before making allegations against it.Kesavan alleged that the Congress leader's remarks about treating women with respect were contradicted by his conduct towards a woman police personnel and a woman journalist."Rahul Gandhi sermonising about treating women with respect is indeed most sadistic and cruel given how Rahul Gandhi in the recent past has misbehaved improperly and inappropriately with both a female police personnel and a woman journalist," Kesavan said.He also questioned Rahul’s response to allegations against a Congress MP facing multiple charges of sexually harassing students."Rahul Gandhi's farcical remarks are highly hypocritical because if Rahul Gandhi truly even had an iota of respect for our women's power, Rahul Gandhi would have squarely condemned and taken action against the Congress MP who is now facing multiple charges of sexually harassing students," Kesavan said.The BJP spokesperson further accused the Congress of failing to advance women's empowerment during its years in power, claiming that the party had not passed the women's reservation Bill despite governing the country for more than 55 years at the Centre."Right from Nehru's Congress to Rahul Gandhi's Congress, the Congress party has always been against women empowerment which is why despite being in power for more than 55 years at the Centre, the Congress party never bothered to pass the women's reservation bill," he said.BJP MLA Ram Kadam also criticised Rahul's remarks, arguing that the Congress leader should verify his claims before making public statements about the RSS."Rahul Gandhi frequently makes remarks about the RSS. While he certainly has the right to engage in political accusations, counter-accusations, and sharp criticism, he should do so only after proper study," Kadam said.Questioning the former Congress president's claim about the organisation's treatment of women, Kadam said the RSS had a women's wing that operated across the country."Is he unaware that the RSS also has a wing for women? It operates across the entire country, and women work within it with the same level of prominence as men," he said.Kadam also questioned whether Rahul was making statements on social media without sufficient information."Are you going to tweet from your X handle based on incomplete information just to grab headlines? At the very least, get your facts straight. Tweeting with such a childish, immature mindset does not befit a leader of the opposition," he said.Telangana BJP state president N Ramchander Rao also accused Rahul of overlooking what he described as the male-dominated nature of the Congress. He challenged the party to explain its record on women's representation and support for the 33 per cent women's reservation proposal."Rahul Gandhi seems to be forgetting how male-dominated his party is. Wherever they are ruling, let him answer how many women chief ministers there are. This BJP has got a woman chief minister in the capital," Rao said.Questioning the Congress's position on women's reservation, he said, "If you are not anti-woman, then why don't you support 33% women reservation with delimitation? Your party failed to pass that legislation in the Parliament several times."Rao also challenged Rahul's claim that women supported his political fight against the RSS, arguing that the Congress's actions did not match its stated position on women's empowerment."Rahul Gandhi has claimed that women are with him, and 'smash patriarchy' is only a slogan for him. But in practice, Congress is against women," he said.Rao also raised the issue of a Congress MP who, he alleged, had been suspended and removed from service at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) over a sexual harassment case."What action have you taken against your own MP who has been suspended and removed from service in JNU over a sexual harassment case?... This is a hypocritical stance of the Congress party," he said.The BJP leaders were responding to a Rahul's post on X on Tuesday, in which the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha described the RSS as an "all-male, anti-constitutional cult" and alleged that it believed women were the property of men."The RSS is an all-male, anti-constitutional cult that believes women are the property of men. I believe in Shiva-Shakti. That's why it gives me such joy to fight them. What's beautiful is that many of their 'own' women are on my side," Rahul wrote.His remarks were the latest in a series of attacks on the RSS. On October 10, the Raebareli MP had accused the Delhi Police of encouraging violence by RSS-BJP supporters against women protesters and young people amid political tensions over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul has also criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, accusing him, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and others of being on the opposing side of his political fight.Separately, the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) also criticised Rahul's comments. VHP national spokesperson Vinod Bansal accused the Congress leader of "mental bankruptcy" and alleged that he was using religion for political purposes."... Leaders like Rahul Gandhi suffer from 'Mental Bankruptcy'. He failed to notice women at RSS events. Vijayadashami celebrations were held across the country yesterday, and I personally attended three of them. Families were present at every event. Congress has travelled the world criticising the RSS, and everyone knows what it has gained or lost in the process..."The remarks came as the RSS held its annual Vijayadashami celebrations at Reshimbagh Ground in Nagpur on Tuesday, during the concluding year of its centenary celebrations.
Article Summary: BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over his remarks accusing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh of gender inequality. Party leaders allege hypocrisy and question Rahul's understanding of the organisation. Telangana BJP state president N Ramchander Rao also accused Rahul of overlooking what he described as the male-dominated nature of the Congress.

Article Title: SC directs Andhra Pradesh poll panel to decide on extending nomination deadline by Thursday
Article Text:
SC asks Andhra poll panel to decide on extending nomination deadline by tomorrow

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission to decide by Thursday whether to extend nomination deadlines for urban local body polls in areas where candidates were allegedly prevented from filing nominations due to law and order issues.The court asked the poll panel to defer publication of the final candidates’ list until October 25 and examine complaints of violence and obstruction by tomorrow. If the commission decides to extend the deadline, candidates must get at least 48 hours from the publication of the decision to file nominations.The court also ordered police protection and CCTV coverage at nomination centres and sought a compliance report. The matter will be heard next on October 27.(With inputs from ANI)

If the commission decides to extend the deadline, candidates must get at least 48 hours from the publication of the decision to file nominations. Article Title: ‘Was it necessary?’: Anupam Kher slams Uttarakhand BJP minister over Daler Mehndi row

NEW DELHI: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has backed singer Daler Mehndi after Uttarakhand cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal confronted him on stage during a cultural event, questioning his performance. Kher criticised the minister's conduct, asking whether it was necessary to publicly humiliate the singer instead of raising concerns privately.“Mantri ji...kya sabke saamne manch par jakar is tarah unhe apmanit karna zaruri tha?” Kher wrote in an Instagram post, expressing disappointment over the way the singer was addressed in front of an audience.The controversy erupted after Mehndi's performance at the annual Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in Tehri Garhwal, Uttarakhand. Uniyal allegedly questioned the singer's presentation, claiming that he appeared disoriented and was lip-syncing. The minister also alleged that Mehndi was drunk.In his post, Kher said he had known Mehndi for several years and was concerned about the singer's health. He said the singer had not been keeping well and deserved to be treated with dignity after decades of contributing to the music industry.“I watched a video in which a minister was speaking to Daler Mehndi ji on stage.The way he spoke to him was deeply upsetting to see. I have known Daler ji for many years. I also know that he hasn’t been keeping well for some time now. Minister ji, you may have had complaints about his performance. You may even have been upset with him. But was it really necessary to go up on stage and humiliate him in front of everyone? Couldn’t the same thing have been said to him privately, with dignity and respect? (Mantri ji. ....kya sabke saamne manch par jakar is tarah unhe apmanit karna zaruri tha?),” Kher wrote.He added that an artist's contribution should be acknowledged and respected, particularly after years of work.“An artist spends an entire lifetime earning the recognition and respect that comes through years of hard work. For the past 30–35 years, Daler ji has brought joy to all of us through his songs. Surely, his contribution deserves some appreciation and respect. Daler ji, I have always known you as a kind-hearted person who spreads love. As far as I know you, you don’t even drink alcohol. I am deeply sorry that you had to go through something like this. ”Earlier, singer Mika Singh came out in support of his brother, saying Mehndi had been unwell for the past two years and had undergone an operation recently. Mika suggested that his health could explain his speech during the performance and rejected allegations that the singer had consumed alcohol.“I know my brother Daler Mehndi, and he does not drink alcohol. He has been unwell for the past two years and is still recovering, yet he continues to perform with his band. These days, many performers use backing tracks, but nobody questions them in the same way,” Mika said.Kher also urged members of the film industry to speak up in support of Mehndi, saying it should not be Mika's responsibility alone to defend his brother.The incident has triggered a debate over the treatment of performers at public events, with Kher questioning why any concerns about Mehndi's performance could not have been raised privately and respectfully.
Article Summary: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has backed singer Daler Mehndi. Uttarakhand cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal confronted him on stage during a cultural event. Kher criticised the minister's conduct, asking whether it was necessary to publicly humiliate the singer instead of raising concerns privately.

NEW DELHI: CBI has officially taken over the murder probe of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, re-registering the case to begin its independent investigation. A special probe team arrived at the Mansa Police Station late last night with a formal letter issued to the police to take over existing records and seizures."As part of the ongoing probe, a CBI team led by a senior DIG will examine the family members of the victim, who are scheduled to reach the Mansa Circuit House Wednesday. Additionally, forensic experts, drug controllers, and other specialists are expected to arrive in Mansa shortly to assist with the investigation," a senior CBI official said.Officials will specifically investigate potential links regarding how banned psychotropic substances were openly sold at chemist shops, sources added.To further this angle, the anti-corruption probe agency will take over documents from the Punjab Police in Mansa and seek the custody of chemist Ashwine Kumar and other individuals.Jhota was murdered on October 13, after being shot during a confrontation at a medical store in Mansa. The Punjab Police claimed to have found in its investigation that the activist was shot dead by chemist Ashwine Kumar during an altercation that was being livestreamed on Facebook.According to the findings, Jhota had confronted the medical store owner over the alleged open sale of banned psychotropic substances and synthetic drugs. The probe revealed that the accused opened fire inside the shop and subsequently followed the injured activist into the street, leading to Jhota's death at Mansa Civil Hospital, before fleeing and later being arrested in Rajasthan.

Article Title: Delhi high court cites national security, junks CIC order to IAF on PMs’ foreign trips
Article Text:
Delhi HC has set aside CIC order directing the IAF to disclose flight records PM Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court has set aside a Central Information Commission order directing the Indian Air Force to disclose flight records pertaining to foreign visits undertaken by PM Narendra Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh, stating such disclosure could compromise national security and the PM’s safety.Allowing a petition by the Central Public Information Officer of Directorate of Personal Services, Air Headquarters, Justice Amit Mahajan held the IAF was justified in denying access to the records under section 8 of RTI that exempts disclosure of information that could jeopardise national security or pose a risk to a person’s life and physical safety.The high court said CIC erred in directing disclosure of Special Flight Returns (SFR-II) after redaction of the names and particulars of security personnel, observing removing such details would not necessarily eliminate the potential security risks.The RTI plea was filed by retired Commodore Lokesh K Batra in 2018, seeking information about foreign visits by Indian PMs on IAF aircraft from April 1, 2013, until the date of his application.In response, the IAF provided certain information about Modi’s foreign travels, and stated there had been no travel by ex-PM Singh on IAF aircraft during the period from April 1, 2013 to May 25, 2014. However, it refused to disclose copies of the SFR, Part-I and Part-II, citing national security concerns and the confidential nature of the records.Batra approached CIC, which directed the IAF on July 8, 2020, to provide certified copies of available and relevant SFR-II records to the applicant.The IAF challenged the CIC order, contending the records contained sensitive information that could potentially enable the identification of security personnel, reveal the composition of PM’s entourage and allow inferences to be drawn about patterns of security deployment.Justice Mahajan said, “The mere fact that public funds have been expended on the foreign visits of the PM does not, by itself, justify disclosure of information which may compromise the security arrangements put in place for such visits.”
Article Summary: Delhi HC has set aside CIC order directing the IAF to disclose flight records PM Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh. Delhi high court said CIC erred in directing disclosure of Special Flight Returns (SFR-II) after redaction of the names and particulars of security personnel.

Article Title: India & United States to boost defence, energy ties, Marco Rubio says trade deal close
Article Text:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US ambassador to India Sergio Gor stand for the national anthem, as they attend a Freedom 250 reception at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar met his US counterpart Marco Rubio in Mumbai, agreeing to further expand cooperation in energy, defence and technology ties and committing to an early conclusion of the trade deal still under discussion.While Rubio emphasised the role that the US can play in the diversification of India's energy and defence supplies, Jaishankar said in a post on X that they also discussed people-to-people ties, alluding to India's concerns over immigration and H-1B governance issues.Speaking at the US anniversary celebrations later, Jaishankar said in Rubio’s presence that Indian talent and skills have helped shape the tech era in the US.The ministers met ahead of a likely meeting between PM Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump next month in Manila on the margins of the ASEAN summit, and also before Modi's visit to the US in December for the G20. Both sides are also working to schedule a Quad leaders’ summit in Manila.A State Department readout said Jaishankar and Rubio discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia. Rubio reiterated that increased energy trade with the US can play a transformative role in diversifying India’s supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand.Rubio’s second visit to India is taking place against the backdrop of US’ Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act meant to penalise countries purchasing Russian oil and Trump’s subsequent suspension temporarily of related tariffs. India maintains that its oil procurement is essential not just for its own energy security but also stability of the global markets. Rubio lauded “substantial progress” made by India in diversifying its energy portfolio.Rubio focused on reducing India's reliance on Russia also in defence as he stressed deepening of defence interoperability, framing enhanced technology purchases by India as a win-win situation for both nations.According to the US readout, Rubio also commended recent progress in bilateral defense and civil nuclear cooperation, and advocated increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both countries.Rubio said in a post on X that he and Jaishankar reaffirmed the importance of advancing the US-India strategic partnership. The ministers will meet again on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta later this month. Both will also join their counterparts from Japan and Australia for a meeting of the Quad foreign ministers in Atlanta.According to the MEA, Jaishankar and Rubio welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India–US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion. Rubio said both sides were “as close as you can be without having an executed agreement”.“I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So, I think that will happen shortly...and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon, and perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter,” said Rubio, addressing the US travelling media.Shortly after his arrival, Rubio laid a wreath at Mumbai’s Taj Mahal Palace Hotel to honor the 26/11 terrorist attacks victims 166 victims, strongly condemning the attacks and reaffirming the US “unwavering solidarity” with the people of India.“Secretary Rubio underscored the Trump Administration’s commitment to dismantling terrorist networks and ensuring that those responsible for acts of terrorism are brought to justice, including individuals facing charges for their roles in planning the 2008 Mumbai attacks,” said the State Department, without naming Pakistan.According to the Indian readout, the visit reflected the sustained momentum of high-level exchanges between the two countries, underscoring the importance both sides attach to further advancing the India-US COMPACT for the 21st century. Modi and Trump had launched the COMPACT (Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology) initiative last year to drive transformative change across key pillars of bilateral cooperation.
Article Summary: Jaishankar and Rubio agreed to further expand cooperation in energy, defence and technology ties. They also discussed people-to-people ties, alluding to India's concerns over immigration and H-1B governance issues. The ministers met ahead of a likely meeting between PM Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump next month.

Malik was placed in the senior tier which deals with planning and target selection,” said another source.This is perhaps why the screenshot in Tiger Shroff case bore the names of Malik and Anmol — the latter is currently lodged in Tihar jail.

Article Title: More trouble for CJP leaders: Another FIR against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka transferred to Crime Branch
Article Text:

CJP leaders move Delhi High Court against custody extension

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has transferred a second FIR registered against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to the Crime Branch, which will now investigate both cases linked to the activists' alleged entry into Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, sources said on Wednesday.Two cases were registered on October 13 following protests by CJP members at the two locations without approval, according to news agency ANI.The case related to Connaught Place was transferred to the Crime Branch on Tuesday, while the second case, concerning Jantar Mantar, has also now been handed over to the unit, sources said.According to news agency PTI, the police alleged that Das, Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and 11 other CJP members entered the Jantar Mantar area on October 13 by trespassing through private premises. Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site.Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened, and all 14 people were detained. Two FIRs were subsequently registered.Meanwhile, Das and Ranka have approached the Delhi High Court challenging an order extending their judicial custody, arguing that their continued detention despite furnishing sureties violates their fundamental right to personal liberty.Their legal team has challenged the October 19 order passed by a Special Executive Magistrate in New Delhi district under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).According to their lawyers, the magistrate rejected fresh sureties submitted by the two leaders on October 19 and directed them to explain why there should not be an apprehension of a breach of peace.The legal team contends that the continued detention is arbitrary and contrary to established legal principles. The leaders have sought the setting aside of the order, arguing that their detention infringes their constitutional right to personal liberty under Article 21.The matter is scheduled to be taken up by the High Court on Wednesday.The leaders sought an urgent hearing on Tuesday, including a night hearing, as the High Court remains closed for the Dussehra vacation.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh said in a post on X, "We have moved the Delhi high court and requested an urgent night hearing. Saurav and Ashutosh should not spend a single minute behind bars. Their liberty must not be curtailed because of political games. Justice must not wait."The party has alleged that bail proceedings have been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two co-convenors, the newspaper reported.According to their legal team, Das and Ranka were first detained on October 10 after arriving at Terminal 3 of the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Preventive proceedings were initiated against them the following day, after which they were released on executing bonds of Rs 50,000 each.They were detained again on October 13 after going to Jantar Mantar carrying the national flag. They were subsequently shown as arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS on October 14.A Special Executive Magistrate sent the two leaders to five-day judicial custody on October 14 for allegedly breaching peace bonds. Their custody was extended by two days on Monday after police sought further detention, citing apprehensions of a breach of peace.
Article Summary: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been in custody since October 10. They are accused of entering Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar without approval. The two leaders are challenging an order extending their judicial custody.

Article Title: Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know
Article Text:
Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio Platforms following its stock market listing.

Jio Platforms IPO:

Jio IPO price band

Jio IPO listing date

India’s largest IPO

Jio IPO GMP

Jio set to be fourth most valuable listed company?

Reliance could topple Tata as India's most valuable group

What Akash Ambani said

About Jio

Anchor book

What brokerages are saying

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms plans to raise approximately Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares.The public issue opens on October 21 and will remain available for subscription until October 23. This marks RIL Group's first IPO in nearly two decades.Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio Platforms following its stock market listing.From Jio IPO price band, listing date to GMP, we take a look at 10 important facts about the Jio IPO and what brokerages are saying:The company has fixed the price band at Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. Based on the offer documents, the IPO values the company at around $108 billion. Investors will be able to apply for Jio Platforms shares in lots of 12, or in multiples of 12 shares.The company is also seeking to widen access to its IPO by setting aside portions of the issue for different investor groups.Eligible Reliance Industries shareholders have a reservation of up to Rs 2,500 crore, while eligible employees can apply under a reservation of up to Rs 500 crore.Retail individual investors will be eligible to subscribe to at least 35 per cent of the net offer.Jio Platforms will list on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) on October 28, 2026.The Jio IPO is expected to surpass Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore IPO in 2024, making it the largest public issue in India's history by value.The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, meaning existing shareholders are not selling their holdings through the offering.Jio’s shares are trading at a grey market premium (GMP) of around 22%, signalling strong interest. On Tuesday, October 20, Jio Platforms shares were quoting at a grey market premium of about Rs 245.GMP refers to the premium that speculators in the unofficial market are prepared to pay for shares of a company awaiting its IPO listing.Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 1,119, this indicates a possible listing price of Rs 1,364, implying a premium of nearly 22%, according to unofficial grey market quotes.Based on the current market capitalisation rankings on the BSE, the company would become India's fourth-most valuable listed company. It would rank behind RIL, valued at Rs 15.9 lakh crore, Bharti Airtel at Rs 11.2 lakh crore and HDFC Bank at nearly Rs 11 lakh crore.The BSE data also showed that Jio Platforms' valuation would be higher than those of ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and TCS. According to this TOI report , Reliance Industries (RIL) Group is poised to displace Tata Group as India's most valuable conglomerate once Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut, marking one of the biggest changes in the country's corporate pecking order in decades.At the upper end of its proposed price band of Rs 1,065-1,119 per share, Jio Platforms is expected to command a valuation of Rs 10.3 lakh crore. This would take the combined market capitalisation of the RIL Group to around Rs 28.5 lakh crore, putting it ahead of Tata Group's Rs 25.5 lakh crore as of October 15, according to ET Intelligence data.Before the proposed listing, RIL Group's market capitalisation stood at Rs 18.2 lakh crore.Adani Group currently occupies the third position among India's largest conglomerates, with a market capitalisation of Rs 17.48 lakh crore. It is followed by HDFC Group at Rs 13.91 lakh crore and Bajaj Group at Rs 13.88 lakh crore.Jio Platforms expects technology, artificial intelligence and cloud computing to fuel its next phase of expansion beyond telecom, Managing Director Akash Ambani told PTI."There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology," Ambani said in an interview with PTI. He pointed to the company's in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform, which serves 533.3 million customers.Satellite connectivity and next-generation 6G technology are among the other areas Jio has identified for future development.According to Ambani, the company's growth prospects are spread across several segments, from mobile services and home broadband to digital solutions for enterprises. He noted that around 26 crore Indians continue to use 2G services, while fixed broadband is available in only about 21 per cent of households across the country.In the decade since Reliance entered the telecom sector, Jio Platforms has built a subscriber base that places it among the world's largest mobile operators.Its operations now extend well beyond mobile connectivity, covering broadband, digital entertainment, cloud computing and enterprise services.Jio Platforms recorded revenue from operations of Rs 1.46 lakh crore in FY26, up from Rs 1.28 lakh crore in FY25. Net profit climbed to Rs 30,049 crore from Rs 26,109 crore over the same period, while EBITDA grew to Rs 76,255 crore from Rs 64,170 crore.Company figures reported for June 2026 show that Jio Platforms had 533.3 million subscribers and accounted for nearly 60% of India's data traffic.The IPO is also expected to improve Jio's financial position. The company plans to use up to Rs 27,500 crore of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings owed by its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.Jio's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio fell to 0.36 times in FY26, compared with 0.88 times in FY24, Akash Ambani said. He added that the IPO would give the company more financial headroom to invest in areas such as 5G, broadband, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and enterprise services.Jio's international technology investors, including Google and Meta, are also expected to contribute to its next stage of growth.Jio Platforms has allotted shares worth Rs 8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at Rs 1,119 apiece, which is the upper end of its IPO’s price band.Institutional bids for the offering crossed a whopping Rs 2.5 lakh crore, which is more than 30 times the value of shares on offer in the anchor book.The company has allocated 7.24 crore shares.The scale of demand points to strong institutional interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO.Life Insurance Corporation of India was the biggest recipient in the anchor allotment, securing shares worth Rs 499.98 crore. New World Fund Inc received shares of Rs 486.27 crore, while the Government of Singapore was allotted Rs 340.93 crore.SBI Focused Fund secured an allocation worth Rs 315 crore, followed by BNP Paribas Financial Markets - ODI, which received shares valued at Rs 303.25 crore.Domestic mutual funds were allotted 2.489 crore shares worth Rs 2,784.96 crore, which is 34.34% of the anchor book.Several major international investment firms also participated in the anchor book. These included BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson.Brokerages have expressed optimism about the offering, pointing to Jio's leading position in the telecom sector, improving profitability and potential for expansion in broadband and artificial intelligence.Motilal Oswal Wealth Management has advised investors to subscribe to the Jio IPO, citing potential listing gains as well as long-term investment prospects. The brokerage pointed to the company's strong position in India's telecom market and its improving earnings performance. It said Jio's extensive subscriber base, in-house technology capabilities and growing broadband business offer a solid platform for further expansion.The brokerage noted that Jio had 533 million subscribers as of June 2026 and accounted for around 60% of India's wireless data traffic. It also sees scope for growth in digital services, backed by Jio's proprietary 5G technology, more than 7,200 patent applications and investments in cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Canara Bank Securities has also recommended subscribing to the issue with a long-term investment horizon. According to the brokerage, Jio stands to gain as customers shift from 2G to 4G and 5G services, home broadband adoption expands and the company explores opportunities to monetise its technology in international markets.Canara Bank Securities identified Jio's in-house technology portfolio, spanning its 5G network, broadband solutions and JioBrain AI platform, as potential drivers of future revenue growth.
Article Summary: India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms plans to raise approximately Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares. Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio.

Article Title: India-New Zealand FTA kicks in: Zero duty, more opportunities - what's in it for India?
Article Text:
India - New Zealand trade deal kicks in

What's in it for India?

1. Duty-free access for Indian exporters

2. A boost for MSMEs and small businesses

3. New opportunities for farmers

4. More opportunities for Indian professionals and students

5. Investment, manufacturing and employment

6. Safeguards for sensitive Indian sectors

7. A larger trade partnership

NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force on Tuesday opening up new opportunities for Indian exporters, manufacturers, farmers, professionals and businesses. The agreement provides 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market for all Indian export tariff lines, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%.Signed on April 27, 2026, the pact aims to deepen economic ties between the two countries and double bilateral trade in goods and services to NZ$7 billion (Rs 35,000 crore) by 2030. Negotiations were launched on March 16, 2025, and concluded on December 22, 2025, within nine months.The agreement is India's 17th operational FTA and the seventh trade pact to come into force in the past five years. It covers goods, services, investment, agriculture, skills and mobility, while retaining safeguards for sensitive sectors.All Indian goods can enter New Zealand duty-free, giving Indian exporters a competitive advantage and placing them on a level playing field with New Zealand's other FTA partners.Textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, automobiles and auto components, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, agricultural products and processed foods are among the sectors expected to benefit.Duty-free access for wooden logs, coking coal and metal waste and scrap will strengthen manufacturing and MSME supply chains. Streamlined regulatory processes are expected to benefit pharmaceutical and medical device industries.The agreement opens New Zealand's market to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), women-led businesses, start-ups, artisans and first-generation entrepreneurs.Zero duties and faster customs processes are expected to reduce landed costs and help Indian businesses expand their customer base. Cooperation will improve access to trade-related information and links with New Zealand's small and medium enterprise ecosystem, with particular attention to businesses owned by women and young people.New Zealand has also committed to facilitating the registration of Indian geographical indications (GIs), creating opportunities to protect products associated with rural artisans and traditional industries.The Agricultural Productivity Partnership will bring technology, training and global best practices to Indian agriculture, extending cooperation beyond tariff concessions.Dedicated action plans for apples, kiwifruit and honey will support better orchard management, reduce post-harvest losses and improve productivity and farm incomes. Cooperation will also cover horticulture, forestry, livestock and fisheries.New Zealand will provide technical assistance to establish Centres of Excellence for kiwifruit, apples and honey. Phase I sites for kiwifruit centres have been identified at Pfutsero in Nagaland and Magra in Uttarakhand. Two apple centres are proposed in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, while honey centres are envisaged in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.Tariff rate quotas for apples, kiwifruit and Mānuka honey are linked to the delivery of action plans and overseen by a Joint Agriculture Productivity Council, linking market access with farmer welfare.New Zealand has offered market access in around 118 services sectors and Most-Favoured-Nation commitments in about 139 sub-sectors, its most extensive services offered under any trade agreement to date.For the first time, dedicated access has been provided for health and traditional medicine services, including Ayurveda, yoga and other AYUSH systems.Indian youth and professionals will have access to 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas annually.There will be no numerical cap on Indian students. Post-study work rights will extend to three years for STEM bachelor's and master's graduates and up to four years for doctoral scholars.New Zealand has committed to facilitating $20 billion in investment into India over more than 15 years.The investment is expected to benefit agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups, supporting innovation, entrepreneurship and employment generation under the Make in India vision.Provisions covering duty-free inputs, bilateral cumulation, customs facilitation and investment promotion could encourage deeper integration into value chains and improve investment conditions.Dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions to protect farmers, dairy producers, fisherfolk and rural communities.Rules of Origin, a bilateral safeguard mechanism and anti-circumvention provisions aim to ensure that benefits reach genuine Indian exporters.Bilateral trade fell about 11% to $1.15 billion in 2025-26, from $1.3 billion in the previous fiscal year. India's exports stood at $566.51 million, while imports were $589.1 million, leaving a trade deficit of $22.59 million.The FTA seeks to reverse the limited scale of trade and expand economic engagement. The first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off at the entry-into-force ceremony, with further product flag-offs planned across agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather.Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said that the agreement would create opportunities for exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and women entrepreneurs. The pact also supports India's strategic partnership with New Zealand and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, with its success ultimately depending on businesses converting improved market access into actual trade and investment.
Article Summary: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force on Tuesday. The agreement provides 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market for all Indian export tariff lines, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%. The pact aims to deepen economic ties between the two countries.

Article Title: India, US ‘perfectly aligned’ on key issues: Marco Rubio; defends ties with Pakistan
Article Text:
Rubio is set to visit Jamnagar for talks on bilateral ties, energy cooperation and commercial investment.

US secy of state defends ties with Pakistan

US secretary of state Marco Rubio urged businesses to view the India-US relationship as a strategic partnership spanning technology, trade and security, saying the two countries were “perfectly aligned” on issues that would shape the 21st century, even as he acknowledged that disagreements between them would persist.Addressing a gathering of India Inc’s leading business figures at a Freedom 250 event at BKC, Rubio said the relationship between the two countries could help shape the future of the global economy, particularly as advances in artificial intelligence and quantum computing transform industries and societies.“I truly believe the relationship between US and India is defining, in many ways, in a positive way, what the 21st century can look like,” he said.The gathering included Noel Tata (Tata Trusts), Anand Mahindra (Mahindra Group), Kiran MazumdarShaw (Biocon), Ashok P Hinduja (Hinduja Group), Amit Dixit (Blackstone), Hitendra Dave (HSBC India), K Balasubramanian (Citi India) and Rahul Badhwar (JPMorgan Chase).Rubio identified emerging technologies and secure trade routes as two areas in which the countries’ interests converge. “US and India are perfectly aligned,” he said, referring to the challenge of harnessing new technologies for public benefit.“We have the same expertise. We have the same talented people working on it, from engineers to creative thinkers and innovators.”He linked economic growth to the security of international shipping routes, arguing that businesses needed the freedom to move goods across borders and reach markets.For India and US, he said, this required “a free and secure Indo-Pacific” in which “no nation can claim dominance or ownership of international shipping lanes”.“No two nations on earth will ever be perfectly aligned on every issue,” he said. “But on the core issues that matter..., alignment between our countries is extraordinary.”The speech did not signal any immediate change in tariffs or market access.Rubio said he believed US should engage more frequently with India, and he planned to return in three months.US is required to have relationships with countries, including with those with whom it may have some disagreements, said secretary of state Marco Rubio while defending ties with Pakistan and condemning terrorism. It could be a positive thing because if... we can speak to them, it perhaps puts us in a position to help discourage the kinds of things India is worried about,” he added.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio urged businesses to view the India-US relationship as a strategic partnership spanning technology, trade and security. Rubio said the two countries were “perfectly aligned” on issues that would shape the 21st century, even as he acknowledged that disagreements between them would persist.

Article Title: US allows mining firm Sherritt to deliver fuel to Cuba
Article Text:
US allows mining firm Sherritt to deliver fuel to Cuba. (File photo)

(From news agency AFP)

HAVANA: Mining company Sherritt, which halted operations in Cuba over US sanctions, on Tuesday said Washington was allowing it to send fuel and other materials needed for nickel extraction to the island.The Canadian firm has mined nickel and cobalt in a joint venture with Cuba's state-owned General Nickel Company S.A. since the 1990s.Tuesday's announcement aims to allow a future resumption of its activities at the Moa mine after US sanctions pushed it to withdraw from the country in early May.Soon afer its withdrawal, however, Sherritt reversed the decision to liquidate its assets and said it was negotiating the sale of 55 percent of its shares with Gillon Capital -- a deal that would make the US firm Sherritt's majority shareholder.Gillon is owned by Ray Washburne, who served as president of the US government's development finance institution during President Donald Trump's first stint in the White House."The Fuel License" granted by the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) "authorizes the sale, transportation, export, delivery and payment for fuel, fuel oil, and sulfur to Moa Nickel, together with all related services," Sherritt stated.Talks with OFAC, the body that doles out Cuba sanctions, took place in close coordination with Gillon Capital, according to Tuesday's statement."The actual restart of operations at Moa Nickel remains subject to receipt of a second OFAC emergency license," it added.Washington imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, allowing only fuel shipments from the US and destined for the private sector to get through.Trump has openly mused about seizing control of the island, claiming that it poses a threat to US national security.
Article Summary: US allows mining firm Sherritt to deliver fuel to Cuba. Canadian firm has mined nickel and cobalt in joint venture with Cuba's state-owned General Nickel Company S.A. since the 1990s. Washington imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, allowing only fuel shipments from the US.

Article Title: Allahabad HC cites long trial, lets off offenders, SC slams ‘misplaced sympathy’
Article Text:
SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A “gracious” trial court and a “very indulgent” Allahabad HC paved the way for two offenders in a grievous hurt case to go scotfree without spending a day in jail on the grounds that they suffered because of a 22-year-long trial, but the courts did not consider the victim, who is still getting treatment, Supreme Court has said.Now, SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said it was a case of misplaced sympathy. The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. SC said the case was “doomed from its inception insofar as justice delivery to the victim is concerned”.“We cannot but, with an amount of consternation, notice the casual manner in which the trial court and the high court considered the issue from the stage of taking cognisance till the release of the accused on application of Probation of Offenders Act. They have gone scot-free without suffering a single day of imprisonment, especially by reason of the misplaced sympathy based on grandiose expositions of law,” it said.The court passed the order on an appeal filed by the brother of the victim, who has lost substantial functionality of both upper limbs.SC said the HC “went overboard” and wondered how it could pass such an order despite the adverse report on the character of the offenders, noting that theywere involved in multiple criminal cases. “True, protracted trial is agonising but here, the accused were on bail and merrily indulging in criminal activities,” the bench said.
Article Summary: The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. Now, SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing. SC said the case was “doomed from its inception insofar as justice delivery to the victim is concerned’

Article Title: ‘Doing a real disservice’: Annamalai backs CJP leaders, questions their continued custody

Article Title: BJP’s delimitation gambit: Will it isolate Congress, puncture opposition’s SIR unity?
Article Text:
Parliament’s Monsoon Session has remained prorogued for 68 days after being adjourned sine die and the opposition has questioned this delay.

A look at how the number of seats may change based on estimates.

Kharge's missives to PM Modi

Rijiju's sharp response to Kharge

Amit Shah dismissed concerns that delimitation would disadvantage southern states.

Why are opposition parties worried

The SIR unity vs Delimitation dilemma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Keen political contest

NEW DELHI: Is the government planning a new delimitation push to puncture the Congress ’s bid to unite the opposition with protests against SIR? Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju has refuelled buzz that Parliament may be called for a short session to take up the legislation while also signalling Congress’s isolation on the issue by rejecting its demands for all-party consultations.The government had tried to push through a Constitution Amendment Bill in April this year in Lok Sabha but failed. The proposed legislation, which aimed at implementing 33% reservation for women in legislatures from 2029 and increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats to 850 did not get the mandatory two-thirds majority. The bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against. It needed support of at least 352 out of the 528 members who were present and voted.The Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13, 2026. It has been 68 days since then. However, the session is yet to be prorogued. This gap has broken the previous record of a 28-day delay for the Monsoon Session in 2015 and has left the opposition, especially the Congress, worried.The Congress fears the government has been engaging in backroom moves with other parties in the opposition camp to cobble up a two-thirds majority and get the two Bills passed.An anxious Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has written four letters to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the last one four days ago. The Congress has been trying to pre-empt a sudden, surprise push by the government to pass the delimitation and women’s reservation bills."You may kindly recall that I had first written to you on April 11, 2026, to convene an All-Party meeting before bringing any Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation. You did not do so. Thereafter, you made the Bills public on the late evening of April 14, 2026 and convened a special session on April 16, 2026. The Constitutional Amendment Bill on Delimitation failed to muster the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17, 2026, by a decisive margin," said Kharge in his letter."Thereafter, on July 16, 2026 and August 27, 2026, I wrote to you again, repeating our request for an All-Party meeting. I am now doing so for a fourth time," the Congress chief said.Kharge cautioned the government against taking a unilateral approach on major constitutional reforms such as national delimitation, which directly affects parliamentary constituency boundaries and regional representation.In a sharp response to Kharge's Oct 16 letter to the Prime Minister, Rijiju said, "When after repeated requests Congress didn't give dates for discussion, govt's outreach extended to other political parties. Consultations were held with representatives of parties including SP, DMK, YSRCP, NCP (SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), AIMIM and BJD with a view to building a broader consensus in support of the proposed legislation. "Rijiju also rejected Kharge’s concerns over the “unprecedented” delay in proroguing the Monsoon session. Dismissing Kharge’s contention, Rijiju cited precedents and underlined that no constitutional requirement existed prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die."The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety or irregularity," Rijiju said.When Parliament is adjourned sine die and not prorogued, it can be convened for a session at short notice. Sine die adjournment means that the session is suspended indefinitely without setting a day for reconvening. It does not mean a formal end of the session, which requires an official prorogation order by the President of India. There is no specific timeframe for prorogation of Parliament after a session has been adjourned sine die. But normally this happens within a few days.Since the Delimitation Bill is a Constitution Amendment Bill and cannot be taken through an ordinance route it makes sense for the government to keep the option alive by not proroguing the session.For the opposition, this is a clear signal that the government is still trying to get the numbers. And that brings us to the second question of opposition unity.The last few weeks have seen the opposition at its united best. The protests against SIR has seen the Congress not just reach out to but also accommodate every opposition party. There have been differences and some reports of one-upmanship, but by and large all parties have been together under the INDIA bloc. The DMK and AAP despite staying away from the opposition coalition’s prorgrammes are united in the cause. In fact, the DMK has sent mixed signals - supporting the agitation against NEET but also accusing the Congress of duplicity citing its support to VIjay and the TVK government in Tamil Nadu. The AAP, on the other hand, has been active with the Cockroach Janata Party and has actively joined their protest programmes. Then there are parties which have been on both sides, like the Shiv Sena (UBT), Mamata Banerjee.In fact, Naveen Patnaik’s Biju Janata Dal of Odisha that normally keeps equal distance from both the NDA and the INDIA bloc also joined one of the protests in Delhi to show solidarity with the cause.And it's not just political parties; several civil society groups have also joined the INDIA bloc platform, amplifying the demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the reversal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has led to huge deletions of voters in several poll-bound states.Interestingly, many political parties named by Kiren Rijiju in his statement have been part of the ongoing protests against SIR under the INDIA bloc. Some that haven’t joined the common protest have expressed solidarity with the cause and have protested separately.This clearly poses a challenge to opposition unity. The Congress and many other opposition parties have been against the SIR and also the Delimitation Bill. However, while many of them are with the Congress on the issue of SIR, their independent negotiations with the government on the Delimitation Bill will keep the grand-old-party worried.The BJP has reached out to several regional parties with an assurance that the proposed delimitation bill will not change the representation of states in Parliament, as the seats in Lok Sabha will be increased 50% across the states and not in proportion to the existing population as it should normally be under the delimitation process.The BJP-led NDA government’s move to tag the women’s reservation bill, which proposes to increase their representation in Lok Sabha, comes as an added pressure as well as incentive. If the parties oppose, they are labelled as anti-women by the BJP and its ruling allies in their respective states. On the other hand, if they accept the proposal, they get the benefit of accommodating additional women without impacting the existing dominance of men.Clearly, this is going to be a keen contest between the BJP and the Congress. It will be interesting to see how the Congress manages to persuade its allies to stay united against BJP’s Delimitation plans. If some regional parties like the DMK, which are very unhappy with the Congress do decide to back the delimitation bill, will it take the sting out of the present SIR campaign?The Congress, anyways, needs to realise that SIR cannot be the only glue that will hold together the opposition parties. The Supreme Court is already hearing a clutch of SIR related petitions. Also, the Election Commission has started the process re-enrolment of voters and also of SSR, the Special Summary revision of electoral rolls, in 14 states and 3 Union Territories. So, SIR as a unifying bond may not help the Congress for long. The main opposition party needs to find lasting ways of ensuring that all its allies are united against the government.
Article Summary: Parliament’s Monsoon Session has remained prorogued for 68 days after being adjourned sine die and the opposition has questioned this delay. Congress fears the government has been engaging in backroom moves with other parties in the opposition camp to cobble up a two-thirds majority and get the two Bills passed.

Article Title: Shinde calls INDIA bloc ‘ten-headed Ravana’, accuses Uddhav of ‘vote theft’

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Tuesday accused Uddhav Thackeray of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly elections and called the INDIA bloc a “ten-mouthed Ravana” whose effigy should be burnt. Addressing his party's Dussehra rally in Mumbai, Shinde attacked the opposition over its allegations of vote theft, accused it of undermining constitutional institutions and said the government would support farmers facing crop losses due to water scarcity.Without naming Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, Shinde alleged that the actual “vote theft” took place after the 2019 Maharashtra assembly elections, when the undivided Shiv Sena joined hands with the NCP and Congress to form a government.“You did not even contest the election. You made a backdoor entry and became chief minister. You stabbed the mandate and grabbed the post. It was a huge dacoity against the people's mandate,” he said.Shinde questioned the opposition's allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls, saying it had earlier raised concerns over an increase in voter numbers and was now questioning the deletion of names.“This is double standards and a daily show of new drama. The INDIA bloc is a ten-mouthed Ravana, and we need to burn its effigy,” he said, accusing the opposition of seeking to undermine the Constitution drafted by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar.He also questioned why the opposition had not alleged vote theft when the INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. “When you lose, you call it vote chori and start alleging foul play. The INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. Why was there no vote chori then?” he asked.Shinde accused the Congress of looting the country for 70 years and alleged that it was now demanding ballot papers after previously winning elections through booth capturing.He also hit out at opposition leaders for their remarks on regime changes in Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, accusing them of encouraging anarchy in India.“This is Hindustan, a new India. This is an India that enters Pakistan,” he said, adding that people would teach a lesson to those he described as anti-national.Questioning the opposition's criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, Shinde said Modi had made India the world's fourth-largest economy and received the highest civilian awards from 36 countries. He also claimed there was no corruption case against the prime minister.“Why use such foul and low language against our PM?” he asked.Shinde further accused opposition leaders of speaking in Pakistan's favour and alleged that their statements were being used to create headlines there. Referring to Captain Smit Machchhar, who saved a plane during an attack, he said the pilot had acknowledged drawing inspiration from Modi.Shinde claimed that Modi, the US president and the Israeli prime minister had congratulated the pilot, while some opposition leaders had not.“Whatever they say here becomes a headline in Pakistan. This is a huge conspiracy...Why do you speak in favour of Pakistan? This is unfortunate. This is sedition and not any kind of love for India,” he alleged.The deputy chief minister also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for organising a rally against the Supreme Court, alleging that it amounted to an insult to the judiciary and an attack on a constitutional institution.“On the one hand, they hold the Constitution in their hands, and on the other, their actions amount to an attack on it. They are moving towards dividing the country,” he said.Taking a swipe at the opposition's demand for the election of the chief election commissioner, Shinde sarcastically asked whether it would also seek elections for the chief justice of India and municipal corporation chiefs.He alleged that opposition parties were promoting a “fake narrative” of vote theft through rallies in Mumbai while farmers were struggling with crop losses.Turning to the agrarian crisis, Shinde said Maharashtra was facing drought-like conditions as standing crops dried up due to a weak monsoon. He announced that he had dispatched an initial 100 tonnes of foodgrains to distressed farmers as an advance Diwali gift, with more consignments to follow.“Today, I have dispatched the first tranche of 100 tonnes of foodgrains to farmers as an advance Diwali gift. There will be more such rounds of assistance given to farmers,” he said.Shinde said excessive rainfall had washed away land last year, causing serious losses to crops and cattle. This year, the monsoon had failed to provide adequate relief to farmers, he added.“Unfortunately, this year, the monsoon turned its back on farmers. We reached out to distressed farmers who are shedding tears and offered them consolation. This is not the time to politicise the farmers' plight but to extend support to them,” he said.Describing himself as a farmer's son, Shinde said he understood the hardships faced by cultivators and their families. He also defended his work on the ground, taking an indirect swipe at his critics.“Let me make it very clear that I don't only give 'bhashan' (speeches), but also give ration to farmers,” he said.
Article Summary: Eknath Shinde accused Uddhav Thackeray of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly elections. He called the INDIA bloc a “ten-mouthed Ravana’ whose effigy should be burnt. The Maharashtra deputy chief minister attacked the opposition over its allegations of vote theft.

Article Title: 'Expect partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism': EAM thanks US for handing over Tahawwur Rana

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday hailed ties between India and the US, saying the partnership between the two countries had grown over the past few decades despite their share of differences.Addressing the Freedom 250 reception in Mumbai, Jaishankar said Indian talent and skills had helped shape the technology era in the US.“Our ties have indeed come a long way. History records that many Americans were supportive of India's struggle for independence. After that, whether it was infrastructure and education or food, agriculture, and technology, our partnership has made a real difference to India's development. Indian talent and Indian skills have helped shape the tech era in the United States. Of course, we've had our share of issues, including the manner in which we approach the world and its challenges,” he said.“But in the last few decades, our partnership has steadily expanded, acquiring new dimensions and new facets. The Quad, Mission 500, Pax Silica, and the Forge Initiative are among some of the notable examples. Growth in the fields of energy, defence, and civil aviation has actually been striking,” he added.Jaishankar also thanked Washington for its decision to extradite Tahawwur Hussain Rana, a key conspirator in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, to India. He said New Delhi expected its partners to show zero tolerance towards terrorism.“Secretary Rubio, all of Mumbai, and indeed all of India, appreciate your laying a wreath today at the Taj Hotel's 26/11 Memorial. India also welcomes this administration's decision to extradite Tahawwur Hussain Rana, who was one of the key culprits. We are clear on our right to defend ourselves against terrorism and expect our partners to show zero tolerance toward terrorism as well,” Jaishankar said.“As we mark this anniversary together, it is natural to reflect on the way ahead. The world order is clearly in transition, and countries are responding accordingly. Each one of us will naturally pursue our national interests. In such an era, expanding our convergence is key to deepening our ties. There are new opportunities in our partnership in trade, investment, technology, and energy, and these await us. We have a shared stake in strengthening peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific. Engaging regularly and identifying common interests will certainly help provide a pathway,” he added.The remarks came as US secretary of state Mark Rubio began a three-day visit to India. Earlier in the day, Jaishankar hosted his US counterpart for wide-ranging talks shortly after Rubio arrived in Mumbai for his second visit to India in less than five months.Following the meeting, Jaishankar said in a social media post that the two had “shared views on further advancement of our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties”.The US state department said the two leaders discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia.“The secretary reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India's supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand,” it said.“He also commended recent progress in bilateral defence and civil nuclear cooperation, and advocated for the increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both our countries,” the state department added.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar hailed ties between India and the US. He said the partnership between the two countries had grown over the past few decades. The remarks came as US secretary of state Mark Rubio began a three-day visit to India.

Article Title: Two Andaman, one Chhattisgarh site added to Unesco World Heritage tentative list
Article Text:
India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

NEW DELHI: Three sites from India have been added to the tentative list of United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization's World Heritage Convention, the Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO announced on Tuesday.The three sites are the Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang and Andaman Subduction Volcanoes in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and the Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape in Chhattisgarh.In a press release dated October 20, the Permanent Delegation of India to Unesco, based in Paris, announced the additions to India's Tentative List under the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.Inclusion on the tentative list is a prerequisite for any property to be considered for nomination to the World Heritage List. The delegation also acknowledged the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for its work in the process.The additions mark a step towards the possible future nomination of the three sites for Unesco World Heritage status.India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including 37 cultural sites, seven natural sites and one mixed site, following the inscription of the ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in July 2026.India ranks sixth globally and second in the Asia-Pacific region.The five countries with the highest numbers are Italy with 62 sites, China with 61, France with 56, Germany with 55 and Spain with 50.India’s first four sites were inscribed in 1983: the Ajanta Caves and Ellora Caves in Maharashtra, and Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal in Uttar Pradesh. These were all cultural sites recognised for their historical, architectural and artistic significance.
Article Summary: The three sites are the Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang and Andaman Subduction Volcanoes in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The additions mark a step towards the possible future nomination of the three sites for Unesco World Heritage status. India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday asserted that human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries, opposing attempts to turn allegations and incomplete statistics into a “negative characterisation” of the world's largest democracy.While speaking at UNGA Third Committee, deputy secretary in the ministry of external affairs Barkha Tamrakar said, "Human rights not to be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting.""India engages with international human rights mechanisms, but such engagement must be based on dialogue, consultation, cooperation with non-selectivity and transparency as guiding principle," she added."We call on delegations to cite the report faithfully, not to inflate a humanitarian communication into a verdict."She also opposed any "attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterisation of the world's largest democracy".Tamrakar's remarks came amid concerns raised by UN human rights experts over recent youth-led protests in New Delhi.On Tuesday, more than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva expressed alarm over what they described as a “repeatedly heavy-handed police response” to peaceful youth-led demonstrations in the national capital.In a statement shared by UN special procedures, the experts alleged that law enforcement agencies had used force against unarmed students, detained protesters arbitrarily and imposed broad restrictions on public gatherings. They called on Indian authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly and ensure accountability for alleged abuses.“Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement has deployed force against unarmed students,” the experts said.The experts said hundreds of thousands of students and their supporters had gathered peacefully across the country to protest government decisions concerning the education system and, more recently, voter-roll deletions.They referred to reports that the deletions affected 130 million individuals, reportedly belonging to Muslim, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities.According to the statement, more than 7,000 young people, journalists, human rights defenders, lawyers and political party members were recently detained in New Delhi and taken to detention centres farther away. Their phones were allegedly seized and protest-related material deleted. Most were released after 24 hours, including protest leaders, the experts said.The statement also cited reports of injuries and ill-treatment among protesters, expressing particular concern over allegations of sexual violence and other forms of gender-based abuse during demonstrations and related detentions.The experts also raised concerns over the reported use of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to impose broad restrictions on public gatherings, suspend public transportation and enforce internet shutdowns.They said restrictions on peaceful assembly must be lawful, pursue a legitimate objective and be necessary and proportionate.They urged Indian authorities to immediately stop the excessive use of force, lift blanket restrictions on assemblies and refrain from the misuse of digital surveillance, including biometric monitoring and internet disruptions.The UN experts called for an independent, impartial and thorough investigation into the conduct of law enforcement personnel and affiliated forces, urging authorities to ensure accountability, justice and reparations for victims.
Article Summary: India says human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries. Remarks come amid UN experts’ concerns over protests in New Delhi. UN experts flag mass detentions, alleged ill-treatment among protesters.

Article Title: AAIB chief gets a year's extension as many key probes, including AI 171, on

NEW DELHI: Govt has granted a one-year extension to Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) director-general G V G Yugandhar, with some key ongoing investigations — including Air India AI 171 crash — awaiting their final reports. The reason: Having a new DG at a time like this could delay the final report into the June 12, 2025, Ahmedabad crash. Accordingly the aviation ministry had recommended an extension for Yugandhar, who retired as Indian Air Force group captain earlier this year, and the same was approved about a month back.The key probes that are currently underway have AI 171 Air India right at the top followed by Air India’s turbulent Phuket-Delhi flight of Aug 4, 2026, and some other crucial cases. AI 171 report is learnt to be in its final stage and will be shared with stakeholders as per rules once ready.People in the know say while the aviation ministry “keeps the aircraft accident investigating agency at an arm’s length and does not interfere in its working in any way,” it is taking steps to strengthen the AAIB. The bureau's lab has been recently upgraded and it now has the capability to download cockpit voice recorder and digital flight data recorder (black box) to know the conversation in the flight deck and the flight parameters till before an event being investigated.It is learnt that the aviation ministry is working on having regional offices of AAIB to ensure investigators reach the site of accident/incident at the earliest. Additionally, this is to augment the bureau’s infra at a time when India’s aviation is seeing a boom right from the number of flight training schools to aircraft in fleet of Indian operators with the figure currently being close to 900.Aurobindo Handa, who was with IAF director (engineering) till Oct 2018 and then joined AAIB as DG on deputation where he remained for 3.5 years, said: “Some steps have been taken to strengthen AAIB but a lot more has to be done. The plan is to have regional offices wherever DGCA has the same. The same must be staffed by non DGCA people to avoid 'conflict of interest'. The investigator’s execution has to be like a clockwork mechanism as its scientific reports pinpointing cause/s of accident/incident are crucial for air safety to prevent the same thing from happening again. And to achieve the outcomes, immaculate staffing is the most important function.”AAIB was formed in 2012 following an ICAO objection that the regulator (DGCA) can’t be the investigator. Till then panels packed with DGCA officials used to conduct probes into accidents and incidents.
